subject: Reasoning
question: In a coded script, वतन = ☆ □ ✚ and नगर = □ ○ △. In the same script, गवत = ?
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Reading the symbol for each letter from the given words — ग = ○ (from नगर), व = ☆ and त = □ (from वतन) — the code for गवत is ○ ☆ □. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which numbers will come in place of the question marks in the following number series? 5, 6, 7, 12, 9, 18, 11, 24, 13, 30, ?, ?
explanation: The right pick is option D. Two alternating series are interwoven: the odd-placed terms 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 rise by 2 (next = 15) and the even-placed terms 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 are the 6-times table (next = 36). So the blanks are 15 and 36.

subject: Reasoning
question: Five children are born at intervals of 3 years. The sum of their ages is 50 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Taking the youngest age as x, the five ages are x, x+3, x+6, x+9, x+12. Their sum 5x+30 = 50 gives x = 4, so the youngest child is 4 years old. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Reasoning
question: Pointing towards Swara, Amit said, 'Her father is the son of my mother's sister'. What is Amit's relation to Swara?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Amit's mother's sister's son is Amit's cousin, and that cousin is Swara's father. So Amit is one generation above Swara — her uncle.

subject: Reasoning
question: In the following number series, what will be the next number? 2, 9, 28, 65, 126, ____.
explanation: The intended answer is option B. Each term follows n³ + 1: 1³+1=2, 2³+1=9, 3³+1=28, 4³+1=65, 5³+1=126, so the next term is 6³+1 = 217.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which of the following figures correctly represents the relation between quadrilateral, rectangle and triangle?

options.A: A small circle lying wholly inside a larger circle, with a separate third circle
options.C: Two overlapping circles together with a third overlapping circle
options.D: Two small circles joined together, with a separate third circle

explanation: The official Set A key selects option A. Every rectangle is a quadrilateral, so the rectangle-circle lies wholly inside the quadrilateral-circle, while a triangle is unrelated and stands as a separate circle. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Reasoning
question: Pointing at a photograph kept on a table, Neeta said 'Her mother is the only daughter of my mother.' It means that the photograph belongs to
explanation: The examiner has marked option D as the correct response. The 'only daughter of my mother' is Neeta herself, so the girl in the photo has Neeta as her mother. The photograph is therefore of Neeta's daughter.

subject: Reasoning
question: The following pie chart shows the details of various expenses incurred in publishing a book (Printing 20%, Promotion 20%, Royalty 15%, Transportation 10%, Binding 20%, etc.). What is the central angle of the sector representing the expenditure on binding?
explanation: This one resolves to option A. Binding is 20% of the total expenditure, and a pie-chart sector's central angle equals that share of 360°: 20% × 360° = 72°. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: In the table below, which letter comes in place of the question mark (?) Row 1: B 1 G 100 ? Row 2: 4 A 49 J 196
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. In each column a letter at alphabet position n is paired with n²: B/4 (2, 2²), A/1 (1, 1²), G/49 (7, 7²), J/100 (10, 10²). Since 196 = 14², the missing letter is the 14th letter, N. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Reasoning
question: A piece of work can be done by 1 man, 3 women and 4 children in 96 hours; by 2 men and 8 children in 80 hours; and by 2 men and 3 women in 120 hours. In how many hours will 5 men and 12 children complete the same work?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Solving the three work equations gives per-hour rates of 1/480 (man), 1/720 (woman) and 1/960 (child). Five men and twelve children together work at 11/480 per hour, finishing in about 43 hours. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Arrange in an appropriate order the Best Performing States in the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Awards, 2025. (a) Rajasthan (b) Chhattisgarh (c) Telangana
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. In the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari Awards 2025, the best-performing states in order are Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan — sequence (c), (b), (a).

subject: Current Affairs
question: Select the correct statement/s: (a) Major Swathi Shanthakumar (Indian Army) was honoured with the UN Secretary General's Award, 2025 in the Gender category for her work on 'Equal Partners, Lasting Peace.' (b) Major Radhika Sen was awarded 'Military Gender Advocate of the Year 2025' by the United Nations Secretariat.
explanation: The right pick is option A. Per the official key only statement (a) is accepted as correct; statement (b) misstates the details of the UN gender-advocate award.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Match the pairs regarding the Lok Sabha Election, 2024 (Political Party – No. of seats won): List I → List II (a) Janata Dal (United) - (i) 29 (b) Telugu Desam Party - (ii) 22 (c) Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam - (iii) 16 (d) All India Trinamool Congress - (iv) 12
explanation: The official Set A key selects option A. 2024 Lok Sabha seats — JD(U) 12, TDP 16, DMK 22 and AITC 29 — giving (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i). Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Current Affairs
question: 'Open AI', an American company, launched which tool related to artificial intelligence in November 2022?
explanation: The intended answer is option C. OpenAI launched the AI chatbot ChatGPT in November 2022. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Which of the following organizations organized the 43rd India International Trade Fair (IITF) - 2024?
explanation: This one resolves to option A. The India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) organises the India International Trade Fair, including the 43rd IITF-2024.

subject: Current Affairs
question: KIRTI (Khelo India Rising Talent Identification) aims to create a sustainable pipeline of athletes to help India become a top 10 sporting nation by ____.
explanation: The examiner has marked option A as the correct response. KIRTI aims to build a pipeline of athletes to make India a top-10 sporting nation by 2036. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Current Affairs
question: 'World Poetry Day' is held each year on ____. It was founded in ____ by ____.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. World Poetry Day is observed on 21 March, established by UNESCO in 1999. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Match the pairs – Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, 2025 (Marathi Language, Author – Book): List I → List II (a) Aditya Davane - (i) Tathagat (b) Sumedh Ingle - (ii) Khol Khol Dushkal Dole (c) Pradeep Kokare - (iii) Mahamaya Nilavanti (d) Chinmay Moghe - (iv) Yuddhanantar
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. The Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar 2025 (Marathi) pairings are (a)-(i), (b)-(iii), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv) per the official list.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Who authored the book 'Ratan N. Tata: The Authorized Biography'?
explanation: The right pick is option D. 'Ratan N. Tata: The Authorized Biography' was written by Thomas Mathew. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Reasoning
question: If coins of Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 are taken in the proportion 3 : 2, how many coins of Rs. 2 will there be in a sum of Rs. 320?
explanation: The intended answer is option C. Let the counts be 3x and 2x. Their value 3x·2 + 2x·5 = 16x = 320, so x = 20 and the number of Rs.2 coins = 3x = 60. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: ABCD is a rectangle and a circle passes through all the vertices of the rectangle. If length of rectangle is 8 cm and breadth 6 cm, the radius of the circle is ____ cm.
explanation: This one resolves to option B. The rectangle's diagonal is the circle's diameter: √(8²+6²) = 10 cm, so the radius is 5 cm. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Reasoning
question: What is the remainder when 5⁵ is divided by 4?
explanation: The official Set A key selects option B. Since 5 ≡ 1 (mod 4), 5⁵ ≡ 1⁵ = 1 (mod 4). (Indeed 5⁵ = 3125 = 4×781 + 1.) So the remainder is 1.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Paradip Port Authority (PPA) was awarded the first prize at the Swachhata Pakhwada Awards 2025 (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways) for outstanding performance in ____.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Paradip Port Authority won the top Swachhata Pakhwada 2025 prize for Cleanliness, Sustainability and Community Participation.

subject: Reasoning
question: Mohan can do a job in 15 days and Rohan in 12 days. With the help of Sameer they finished it in 4 days. How many days will Sameer alone take?
explanation: The examiner has marked option A as the correct response. Mohan and Rohan together do 1/15 + 1/12 = 3/20 of the work per day; the team does 1/4 per day, so Sameer does 1/4 − 3/20 = 1/10 — i.e. 10 days alone. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: What is the addition of all even natural numbers from 1 to 101?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. The even numbers 2 to 100 sum to 2(1+2+…+50) = 2×1275 = 2550.

subject: Reasoning
question: A hall is 15 m long and 12 m broad. If the sum of the areas of the floor and ceiling equals the sum of the areas of the four walls, then the volume of the hall is
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Floor + ceiling = 2×(15×12) = 360; the four walls = 2h(15+12) = 54h. Equating gives h = 20/3 m, so the volume = 180 × 20/3 = 1200 m³.

subject: Reasoning
question: Solve: √(10 + √(25 + √(108 + √(154 + √225))))
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Working from the innermost radical: √225 = 15; √(154+15) = √169 = 13; √(108+13) = √121 = 11; √(25+11) = √36 = 6; √(10+6) = √16 = 4. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Reasoning
question: 'A' purchased an item for Rs. 400 and sold it to 'B' at 10% profit. 'B' sold it to 'C' at 20% loss, and 'C' sold it to 'D' at 25% profit. At what price did 'D' purchase the item?
explanation: The right pick is option C. 400 → +10% → 440 (B buys); → −20% → 352 (C buys); → +25% → 440, so D pays Rs.440. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: A bar graph published by Reuters shows the minimum and maximum estimated numbers of three near-extinct species. Minimum — Red Wolf 20, Puerto Orange-bellied Parrot 20, Ornate Ground Snake 10; Maximum — Red Wolf 31, Puerto Orange-bellied Parrot 26, Ornate Ground Snake 51. Taking the average of the minimum and maximum for each species, which species has the least number?

options.D: All species have the same average

explanation: The intended answer is option B. Averages: Red Wolf (20+31)/2 = 25.5, Puerto Orange-bellied Parrot (20+26)/2 = 23, Ornate Ground Snake (10+51)/2 = 30.5. The least is the Parrot.

subject: Reasoning
question: A student scored a total of 380 marks in Science, Maths and English, in the ratio 5 : 10 : 4 respectively. How many marks did the student score in Maths?
explanation: The official Set A key selects option A. The total 380 is split in the ratio 5:10:4 (sum 19), so Maths = 10/19 × 380 = 200 marks. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Reasoning
question: A boat takes 6 hours to travel 36 km downstream and 9 hours to travel the same distance upstream. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
explanation: This one resolves to option A. Downstream speed = 36/6 = 6 km/h and upstream = 36/9 = 4 km/h, so the speed in still water = (6+4)/2 = 5 km/h. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Reasoning
question: A pie chart shows the distribution of a company's employees across 5 locations in Maharashtra — A 15%, B 25%, C 30%, D 9%, E 21% — with a total of 6500 employees. How many more employees are at A and E together than at C?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B as the correct response. A and E together = 15% + 21% = 36%; C = 30%. The difference is 6% of 6500 = 390.

subject: Polity
question: As per the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, the Chief Commissioner and the Commissioners shall hold office: (a) for a term of four years, or (b) for a term of five years, or (c) until they attain the age of sixty-five years, (d) shall not be entitled for reappointment.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Under the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015 the Chief Commissioner/Commissioners hold office for five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier — statements (b) and (c). Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Polity
question: As per Section 29(1) of the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015, which specific power has been given to the State Government?

options.A: Power to protect actions of its officers taken in good faith
options.D: Power to bar jurisdiction of any other court

explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Section 29(1) of the Maharashtra Right to Public Services Act, 2015 is the classic 'power to remove difficulties' clause: if any difficulty arises in giving effect to the Act, the State Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make provisions not inconsistent with the Act to remove that difficulty. Option A (protection for good-faith acts), option C (repeal of ordinances) and option D (bar of court jurisdiction) are different legal ideas and are not what Section 29(1) confers. So lock the pair: Section 29(1) → power to remove difficulties.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following statements does NOT come under Article 164?

options.A: The Chief Minister shall be appointed by the Governor.
options.B: The other Ministers shall be appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
options.C: The Governor shall be appointed by the President.
options.D: The Cabinet shall be collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

explanation: The right pick is option C. Appointing the Governor is done by the President under Article 155, not Article 164, so that statement does not belong to Article 164.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following State Legislative Assemblies do NOT have reserved seats for Scheduled Tribes? (a) Tamil Nadu (b) Punjab (c) Uttar Pradesh (d) Goa
explanation: The official Set A key selects option A. The Punjab and Goa legislative assemblies have no seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes — statements (b) and (d). MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Polity
question: Match the pairs (Chief Minister – Tenure): List I → List II (a) Shankarrao Chavan - (i) 1975-1977 (b) Vasantdada Patil - (ii) 1977-1978 (c) Manohar Joshi - (iii) 1991-1993 (d) Sudhakarrao Naik - (iv) 1995-1999
explanation: This one resolves to option B. CM tenures — Shankarrao Chavan 1975-77, Vasantdada Patil 1977-78, Manohar Joshi 1995-99 and Sudhakarrao Naik 1991-93 — give (a)-(i), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii).

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following are compulsory provisions of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992? (a) Organisation of Gram Sabha in a village or group of villages. (b) Establishment of Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels. (c) Endowing the Gram Sabha with powers and functions at the village level. (d) 21 years to be the minimum age for contesting Panchayat elections.
explanation: The examiner has marked option C as the correct response. The compulsory provisions of the 73rd Amendment include organising the Gram Sabha, three-tier Panchayats and a minimum contesting age of 21 — (a), (b), (d).

subject: Polity
question: Select the correct statements about citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. Every person who has his domicile in India and — (a) was born in the territory of India; (b) either of whose parents was born in the territory of India; (c) who has been ordinarily resident in India for not less than seven years immediately preceding such commencement — shall be a citizen of India.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. For citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (Article 5), the key accepts domicile with birth in India (a) or a parent born in India (b); the 'seven years' residence in (c) is inaccurate. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments are related to Fundamental Duties? (a) 42nd Amendment (b) 44th Amendment (c) 84th Amendment (d) 86th Amendment
explanation: The right pick is option C. Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment and expanded (the right/duty of education) by the 86th Amendment — (a) and (d). The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Polity
question: Match the following (Committee – Date): List I → List II (a) Vasantrao Naik Committee - (i) 1977 (b) Ashok Mehta Committee - (ii) 26 June 1960 (c) Bongirwar Committee - (iii) 18 June 1984 (d) P.B. Patil Committee - (iv) 2 April 1970
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. (a) Vasantrao Naik Committee-26 June 1960, (b) Ashok Mehta Committee-1977, (c) Bongirwar Committee-2 April 1970, (d) P.B. Patil Committee-18 June 1984, i.e. (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii).

subject: Polity
question: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for the suspension of fundamental rights during a national emergency?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Article 359 provides for suspension of the enforcement of fundamental rights during a national emergency. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Polity
question: Select the correct statement/s: (a) A member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly may be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly. (b) No resolution for the purpose of Article 179 clause (c) shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move it.
explanation: The intended answer is option C. Both statements — removal of the Speaker/Deputy Speaker by a majority of all members and the 14-day notice under Article 179 — are correct. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Polity
question: The Council of Ministers in states having large tribal populations are mandated to include one minister for tribal affairs (Article 164(1)). (a) Maharashtra (b) Tamil Nadu (c) Orissa (d) Madhya Pradesh (e) Bihar (f) Punjab
explanation: The official Set A key selects option C. Article 164(1) mandates a Minister for tribal welfare in Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and (earlier) Bihar — statements (c), (d), (e).

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following is NOT guaranteed under Article 19 of the Constitution?

options.A: Right to freedom of speech and expression
options.B: Right to assemble peacefully and with arms
options.C: Right to form associations or unions or co-operative societies
options.D: Right to move freely throughout the territory of India

explanation: This one resolves to option B. Article 19 protects the right to assemble peacefully and 'without arms', so the option stating 'with arms' is not guaranteed.

subject: Polity
question: Select the correct statements about Article 20 – Protection in respect of conviction for offences. (a) No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once. (b) No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself. (c) No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the act, nor be subjected to a greater penalty than that in force at that time.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Article 20 protects against double jeopardy and self-incrimination; per the official key the matched statements are (a) and (b). Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: Polity
question: Select the correct and incorrect statement/s: (a) The reports of the CAG of India relating to the accounts of the Union shall be submitted to Parliament. (b) The reports of the CAG of India relating to the accounts of a State shall be submitted to the Legislature of the State.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D as the correct response. Per the official answer key, the two statements as set in the paper are treated as incorrect. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Polity
question: Select the correct statements about the Councils of Ministers of the NCT of Delhi and Puducherry (appointment, tenure and responsibility to the legislature). (a) The Chief Minister is appointed by the President and the other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister. (b) The Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. (c) The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the Union Territory.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. Under Art. 239AA (Delhi) and the UT Act framework (Puducherry), the CM and other Ministers are appointed by the President (others on the CM's advice), they hold office during the pleasure of the President, and the Council is collectively responsible to the UT Legislative Assembly — so (a), (b) and (c) are all correct.

subject: History
question: Which of the following social reformers is primarily mentioned as having worked for the upliftment of farmers?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Mahatma Jyotirao Phule worked extensively for the upliftment of farmers (as in 'Shetkaryacha Asud'). The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: History
question: Which of the following societies was revitalized by Chh. Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur? (a) Samata Samaj (b) Prarthana Samaj (c) Arya Samaj (d) Satyashodhak Samaj
explanation: The intended answer is option D. Chh. Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur revitalised the Satyashodhak Samaj.

subject: History
question: Through which newspaper(s) did Bhau Mahajan write on social issues? (a) Dhumketu (b) Vartaman Dipika (c) Dnyan Darshan (d) Sudharak
explanation: The right pick is option A. Bhau Mahajan wrote on social issues chiefly through (a) Dhumketu and (c) Dnyan Darshan. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: History
question: Which of the following descriptions is correct regarding the book 'Asprushyanchi Kaifiyat'? (a) Mahatma Phule wrote the booklet. (b) It contains accounts of the atrocities against the Untouchables. (c) Mahatma Phule presented it to Queen Victoria. (d) It told Queen Victoria that British officials were responsible for the injustice against the Untouchables.
explanation: The official Set A key selects option B. Mahatma Phule wrote 'Asprushyanchi Kaifiyat' recounting the atrocities against Untouchables — statements (a) and (b); the Queen Victoria claims are not accepted.

subject: History
question: Who is known as the father of the Labour Movement in India?
explanation: This one resolves to option C. Narayan Meghaji Lokhande is regarded as the father of India's labour movement. Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: History
question: What was the main objective behind Vasudev Balwant Phadke's acts of looting the houses of wealthy people?

options.A: To collect funds required for an armed rebellion against the British government.
options.B: To accumulate wealth for personal luxury.
options.C: To create fear in society and gain popularity.
options.D: To gain immediate control of political power.

explanation: The examiner has marked option A as the correct response. Vasudev Balwant Phadke looted the houses of the wealthy to raise funds for an armed revolt against British rule. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: History
question: Which of the following leaders had to serve four months in Dongari Jail in the Kolhapur Barve case? (a) Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak (b) Gopal Ganesh Agarkar (c) Gopal Krishna Gokhale (d) Vishnushastri Chiplunkar
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. In the Kolhapur Barve case, Tilak and Agarkar were jailed for four months — statements (a) and (b).

subject: History
question: Match the following (Organisation – associated fact): List I → List II (a) Prarthana Samaj - (i) Khandbandi Movement (b) Satyashodhak Samaj - (ii) A college of higher education at Kolhapur (c) Arya Samaj - (iii) Kolhapur and Satara were centres of influence (d) Pune Sarvajanik Sabha - (iv) Establishment of the 'Arya Mahila Samaj'
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Matching — (a) Prarthana Samaj-(iv) Arya Mahila Samaj, (b) Satyashodhak Samaj-(iii) Kolhapur/Satara influence, (c) Arya Samaj-(i) Khandbandi movement, (d) Pune Sarvajanik Sabha-(ii) college at Kolhapur. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: History
question: Who among the following contributed to the development of economic nationalism? (a) Bhaskar Pandurang Tarkhadkar (b) Ramkrishna Vishwanath (c) Bhau Mahajan (d) Mahadev Govind Ranade
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Economic nationalism was developed by Tarkhadkar, Ramkrishna Vishwanath, Bhau Mahajan and Ranade — all four. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: History
question: Which is the Marathi mouthpiece of the Workers and Peasants Party in Mumbai?
explanation: The right pick is option A. 'Kranti' was the Marathi mouthpiece of the Workers and Peasants Party in Mumbai.

subject: Geography
question: Match the river and the dam on it: List I → List II (a) Krishna - (i) Chandoli (b) Warna - (ii) Kanher (c) Bhogavati - (iii) Dhom (d) Venna - (iv) Radhanagari
explanation: The official Set A key selects option B. River-dam pairs — Krishna-Dhom, Warna-Chandoli, Bhogavati-Radhanagari, Venna-Kanher, i.e. (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii). Practising the exact reasoning behind the correct option is worth easy marks in the paper.

subject: Geography
question: In which State of India is the North Similipal Tiger Reserve located?
explanation: The intended answer is option A. The North Similipal Tiger Reserve is located in Odisha.

subject: Geography
question: Consider the following statements: (a) Due to afforestation, the upper layer of the soil is eroded and the groundwater table decreases. (b) Due to deforestation, the upper layer of the soil consolidates and raises the groundwater table. (c) Alkaline soils in arid and semi-arid regions of India are becoming fertile due to increased sodium, calcium and magnesium content. Which of the above statements is/are wrong?
explanation: This one resolves to option D. Statements (a) and (b) reverse the true effects of afforestation and deforestation, and (c) is also incorrect — so all three are wrong. Add this to your one-page revision notebook; it resurfaces across prelim cycles.

subject: General Studies
question: Identify the wrong pairs (Organisation/Conference – Place): (a) World Wildlife Fund – Switzerland (b) United Nations Environment Programme (1972) – Stockholm (c) Centre for Science and Environment – Bhopal (d) World Earth Summit (1992) – Oslo
explanation: The examiner has marked option C as the correct response. Wrong pairs — the Centre for Science and Environment is in New Delhi (not Bhopal) and the 1992 Earth Summit was at Rio de Janeiro (not Oslo) — (c) and (d).

subject: Reasoning
question: Consider the following statements regarding the decentralized framework under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002: (a) State Biodiversity Boards have the statutory authority to approve commercial utilization of bio-resources by foreign individuals and multinational corporations. (b) Local Biodiversity Management Committees are empowered to levy collection fees on any person accessing bio-resources from their territorial jurisdiction. (c) The National Biodiversity Authority is not bound by directions given by the Central Government. Which of the statements is/are correct?
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 only statement (b) — that Biodiversity Management Committees may levy collection fees — is correct. The three wrong options are close-fitting distractors, so re-read the stem once before finalising.

subject: Geography
question: According to the India State of Forest Report - 2023, which of the following classes of forest has the highest area in Maharashtra?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Per the India State of Forest Report 2023, Open Forest occupies the largest area in Maharashtra. MPSC revisits this point in some form every couple of prelim cycles.

subject: Geography

subject: Reasoning
question: तीन वर्षांच्या अंतराने जन्मलेल्या 5 मुलांच्या वयांची बेरीज 50 वर्षे आहे. तर सर्वात लहान मुलाचे वय किती?
explanation: थेट उत्तर — पर्याय A. सर्वात लहान वय x धरल्यास वये x, x+3, x+6, x+9, x+12; बेरीज 5x+30 = 50 ⇒ x = 4 वर्षे. तीन चुकीचे पर्याय जवळपासचे विचलक आहेत, म्हणून अंतिम करण्यापूर्वी स्टेम पुन्हा वाचा.

subject: Reasoning
question: खालील संख्याश्रेणीमध्ये पुढील संख्या कोणती असेल? 2, 9, 28, 65, 126, ____.
explanation: अपेक्षित उत्तर पर्याय B. प्रत्येक पद n³+1 आहे (2, 9, 28, 65, 126), म्हणून पुढील पद 6³+1 = 217.
